newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bankers to file court motion on credit unions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bankers to file court motion on credit unions.

text.p: Banking trade groups said Monday they planned to file a motion in U.S. District Court seeking to nullify National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) regulatory changes passed last week.
The motion was expected to be filed later Monday on behalf of the American Bankers Association, the Independent Bankers Association of America and America's Community Bankers.
The NCUA, which is the federal regulator of credit unions, held an emergency meeting last week at which it approved changes to rules governing membership policy.
The NCUA changes were effective immediately and included allowing employees of different companies to belong to the same credit union if the companies were in related fields.

A draft of the bankers' motion said the NCUA interim regulation was contrary to prior court orders and did not follow proper procedure of issuing public notice and giving an opportunity for public comment.
"The (NCUA) Board's interim policy is well within the parameters of the Appeals Court's July 30 decision," NCUA Chairman Norman D'Amours said in a statement.
